## Household and background

Rio Blackwood (born December 14, 1975) is single with no dependents and lives at 18 Mesa View Drive in Anytown. Rio is a licensed land surveyor at Meridian Land Survey Associates — one W-2, box 1 wages $52,847.00, box 2 federal withholding $6,480.00 (extra withholding elected to cover the royalty tax).

Rio inherited a fractional mineral interest in the family ranch from a grandfather; Caprock Basin Energy Partners operates the wells and paid $18,240.00 of oil & gas royalties this year (Form 1099-MISC box 2). Rio's own records show $1,610.00 of related expenses — county ad valorem assessments on the mineral interest and a division-order title fee. As a royalty owner Rio claims PERCENTAGE depletion (15% of gross income from the property); no cost depletion schedule exists for the inherited interest.

## Interview

**Q.** What kind of royalty is this — mineral, book, patent?

**A.** Oil and gas — a small inherited share of the wells on my grandfather's ranch. The well operator pays quarterly.

**Q.** Do you have a cost-depletion schedule for the interest?

**A.** No — it came to me by inheritance and I've never computed a cost basis for depletion. My preparer takes the 15% percentage depletion each year.

**Q.** What are the $1,610 of expenses?

**A.** The county assesses the mineral interest separately, and I paid a title company to fix a division order. Those are my records — not on the 1099.

**Q.** Any dependents? Could anyone claim you as a dependent? Are you blind, disabled, or a student? A U.S. citizen all year?

**A.** No to all of those, and yes — citizen all year.

## Preparer notes

- Oil/gas royalty ⇒ §613A PERCENTAGE depletion, engine-computed: 15% × 18,240 = 2,736, capped at net property income (18,240 − 1,610 = 16,630 — the cap does not bind); no taxpayer cost depletion, so the greater-of takes 2,736 (Schedule E line 18). Net royalty = 18,240 − 1,610 − 2,736 = 13,894.
- Total income $66,741; taxable income $50,991; withholding $6,480 → a small refund.
